01About us

Firm Overview

Aemulus Advisory is an operational and business efficiency consultancy. We help organisations run leaner, waste less and get full value from every project and investment, both the financial returns and the non-financial gains such as safety, quality, capability and customer confidence.

Our method is benefits realisation: the discipline of defining what a change should deliver, assigning ownership, tracking it and proving it. Our particular focus is Northern manufacturing, making sure the new machine, the ERP system, the automation line or the energy upgrade makes your processes more efficient, and that you can show your board and your bank that it has.

Define · Own · Track · Review

How We Work

Efficiency gains do not happen by themselves. We use benefits realisation, a proven discipline from major public programmes, to turn every process change into measurable improvement. Four steps, every engagement, so value is planned for, owned and checked rather than hoped for.

01

Define

What does success look like, in numbers?

Before money is spent, we set specific targets: reduce scrap from 8% to 5% in 12 months, not "improve efficiency". Financial and non-financial benefits alike.

02

Own

Who in the business is accountable?

Every benefit gets a named owner who will still be there after the project team has moved on.

03

Track

What has changed since last month?

A simple register of what was promised, what was measured and what was achieved. Updated monthly, reported to the board alongside the financials.

04

Review

Did it deliver what the business case said?

An honest look back at 6 and 12 months. If it delivered, that evidence strengthens the next case. If not, the learning stops the same mistake twice.

02Where efficiency shows up

Financial and Non-financial

Financial

Efficiency savings

Cost taken out of operations: energy, labour hours, scrap, rework and procurement. Named, measured and tracked every month.

Financial

Investment returns

What equipment, automation, ERP and change programmes delivered against the business case that justified them.

Financial

Revenue protection

Revenue kept through better delivery and quality: on time and in full, fewer returns, customers retained.

Non-financial

Quality and safety

Fewer defects, fewer incidents, stronger compliance. Benefits that protect the business even when they never appear on the P&L.

Non-financial

People and capability

Skills embedded, processes adopted, teams who own their results. The change that makes the financial benefits last.

Non-financial

Customer and carbon

Customer satisfaction, supplier standing and progress towards net zero, measured so they count when the board decides.

03Services

What We Do

Senior, practitioner-led support to improve operational and business efficiency, delivered through benefits realisation at every stage of a change, from the business case to the final review. Each engagement is scoped to your organisation, so you only pay for what you need.

  • Efficiency Health Check

    A rapid diagnostic of where your operations are losing time, money and capacity, and how well your investments are tracked, with a board-ready report on the gaps and what to fix first.

  • Efficiency Starter Pack

    The foundations for lasting improvement: a benefits realisation framework, a benefits register, a benefits map and a clear ownership model.

  • Efficiency Improvement Programme

    An embedded lead for three to six months who drives process improvement through benefits realisation: delivery governance, a live dashboard and monthly reporting to your board.

  • Business Case Development

    Evidence-based investment cases that boards, lenders and funders believe, with benefits defined before the money is spent.

  • Benefits Realisation Workshop

    A one-day, in-house session that teaches your team how to define, own and track efficiency benefits for themselves.

Coming next: an AI-assisted diagnostic and benefits dashboard, built on the same methodology, for organisations that want to track value themselves.

04Manufacturing

Northern Manufacturers

Efficiency is where Northern manufacturers win or lose margin. Ask an MD what the last major investment cost and you will have a figure in seconds. Ask what it did for throughput, scrap or energy use and most cannot say. We close that gap, so processes improve and the next investment decision rests on evidence rather than gut feel.

  • iIs the thing you spent money on working?
  • iiIf not, why not, and who owns fixing it?
  • iiiWhat are your energy, labour and waste costs doing since the change?
  • ivWhat are you about to spend on, and should you?

06The founder

Bamidele Thomas

An operational and business efficiency specialist with over 30 years across the City, the United Nations, international consulting and UK public sector delivery. Benefits realisation is the method at the heart of every Aemulus engagement.

He started as a junior fixed-income trader in the City of London, then spent 13 years with UNDP: senior policy adviser to the head of the Regional Bureau for Africa, policy adviser to the Resident Representative in Malawi, and adviser on the Results-Based Management System reform. As a consultant in Africa and Europe, alongside the World Bank, the EU and FCDO, he advised Nigeria's central government on economic reform and on foreign direct investment in telecoms, oil and gas, and agriculture.

UNDPWorld BankEuropean UnionFCDO

In the UK he has led benefits work across policing, environmental regulation and central government. He co-authored a practitioner book on benefits realisation and writes the weekly Beyond the Phantom series on LinkedIn. The thread throughout: measuring results, not activity.

08Insights

The Aemulus Brief

Briefing · October 2026

Investment is moving North. Evidence will decide who gets the next round.

Since Andy Burnham became Prime Minister on 20 July 2026, the North has moved closer to the centre of economic policy. Number 10 North, a Manchester office working alongside Downing Street, now coordinates economic strategy and local growth work across northern England.

Stated plans include a 10-year industrial plan with regional ambitions, local good growth funds pooling public and private investment, and procurement that favours British suppliers. A Treasury roadmap on fiscal devolution is due alongside the autumn budget.

The government has kept the existing fiscal rules. More money will be steered North under tight limits, so every pound will be asked what it returned. Manufacturers who can show the benefits of their last investment will be best placed for the next.

Sources: Premiership of Andy Burnham · TIME · Al Jazeera
